newsitem.title: USA: Frontier Airlines sets takeover provision.
newsitem.headline: Frontier Airlines sets takeover provision.

text.p: Frontier Airlines Inc said Thursday its board of directors had adopted a provision to defend the company from a take-over bid.
As part of the provision, the board declared a dividend distribution of one common stock purchase right on each outstanding share of its common stock, it said.

The company said the rights would become exercisable if a third party, without Frontier's prior consent, acquired shares representing 20 percent or more of its common stock, or announced a tender offer that would result in such an ownership. The board has the right to reduce the 20 percent ownership threshold to no less than 10 percent, it said.
"The provision was adopted as a protective measure in light of analyst predictions of future consolidations and other uncertainties in the airline industry," it said.
"To our knowledge ...there are no Frontier takeover proposals pending, nor are any contemplated," it added.
The company said it will make the dividend distribution of rights on March 15 to shareholders of record on the same date. Rights will expire on February 20, 2007, it said.
Each right entitles Frontier's shareholders to buy one share of common stock at an exercise price of $17.50.
Frontier had 8.9 million shares outstanding as of February 19.
